prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Company news: REIT, homebuilder and utility.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed REIT, homebuilder and utility companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **KBH** / **LEN** — Homebuilders

- A report published October 2 described U.S. housing conditions as a “soft period” as mortgage rates exceeded 7%; KB Home executive chairman Jeffrey Mezger said conditions had weakened since the company’s June earnings report, while Lennar executive chairman Stuart Miller said the operating environment had deteriorated since its prior earnings call. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 20:30 ET)[4]
- KB Home reported third-quarter revenue of **$1.297 billion** and EPS of **$1.05**; the available report did not provide consensus estimates or a new-versus-old guidance comparison. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 20:30 ET)[4]
- Lennar reported third-quarter revenue of **$8.05 billion** and EPS of **$1.19**; the available report did not provide consensus estimates or a new-versus-old guidance comparison. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 20:30 ET)[4]
- KB Home said its construction time had declined to **99 days**; Lennar said construction costs per square foot improved **1% sequentially** and **6% year over year**, while cycle time fell to **116 days** from **121 days** in the prior quarter. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 20:30 ET)[4]
- Lennar’s average sales incentive rate was approximately **12%** in the third quarter; KB Home said built-to-order homes represented **74%** of third-quarter deliveries. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 20:30 ET)[4]
- Lennar shares were reported lower after short seller **Hunterbrook** raised concerns about the homebuilder; the available result did not state the percentage move or the publication time of the short-seller report. [rumor] (Indy Finance, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[7]

## **HHH** — REIT / Real Estate

- Howard Hughes Holdings rose **3.8%** during the week ended October 2 while the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF declined **1.5%**; the available source did not identify a company-specific announcement during the requested window. (Citybiz, Oct. 5, 09:52 ET)[1]

## **NLY** — Mortgage REIT

- Annaly Capital Management declined **10%** during the week ended October 2; the available source did not identify a company-specific announcement during the requested window. (Citybiz, Oct. 5, 09:52 ET)[1]

## **RITM** — REIT

- Rithm Capital and DRA Advisors announced the closing of a joint venture to own **1301 Avenue of the Americas** in New York City through Rithm’s real-estate operating platform, Elecor Properties; the available result did not provide the announcement’s exact publication time. (Business Wire, Oct. 2, time not provided)[2]

## **JAN** — REIT

- Janus Living announced that it will release third-quarter 2026 results after the market close on **Monday, November 2, 2026**, followed by a conference call and webcast at **12:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026**. (Business Wire, Oct. 2, time not provided)[2]

## Real Estate / Mortgage — Sector Data

- The average U.S. 30-year fixed mortgage rate reached **7.28% on October 1**, described as a three-year high; the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF fell **1.5%** for the week ended October 2, while office REITs fell **4.7%** and health-care REITs rose **0.6%**. (Citybiz, Oct. 5, 09:52 ET)[1]
- The 10-year Treasury yield reached **5.29%**, its highest level since **2002**, in a market report published October 2; the item characterized homebuilders, utilities, and REITs as interest-rate-sensitive sectors. (247WallSt, Oct. 2, 07:15 ET)[5]

## Analyst Actions

- No qualifying U.S.-listed REIT, homebuilder, or utility analyst rating or price-target change with both old and new values was identified in the available search results for the requested window.
